## Summary
"General Electric Consumer and Industrial" is the name of a GE division that existed from January 2004, when GE Consumer Products merged with GE Industrial Systems, and whose appliance half became today's GE Appliances, sold to Qingdao Haier (now Haier Smart Home) on 6 June 2016 for $5.6 billion with the GE name licensed through 2056 [1]. The division name survives only in the IEEE registry: the single MA-L block D8:28:C9 is listed to "AP35-1405, Louisville KY 40225" [2][3], and Appliance Park in Louisville is GE Appliances' headquarters and largest plant [1][6], so the block is read here as GE Appliances' (the "AP" = Appliance Park reading is an inference from the address, not a documented fact). A MAC in this block is a kitchen or laundry appliance, water heater or air conditioner on GE's SmartHQ platform, either with Wi-Fi built in or via the optional Connect Module [4]; the company claims the first full suite of Wi-Fi connected appliances and nearly 16,000 US employees under the "GE Appliances, a Haier company" name [6]. The SmartHQ Connect Module PBX23W00Y0 is listed as no longer manufactured and integrates with Alexa, Google Assistant, IFTTT, Nest and Sonos [5], so an operator should expect these devices to hold outbound cloud sessions to GE/Haier services and third-party assistants. The band, 802.11 generation and the Wi-Fi chipset are not stated on the GE pages reached, and the FCC ID mirrors (fccid.io, fcc.report) refused the fetch, so silicon and the FCC grantee code are left unknown rather than guessed; the single 2015-updated block [2] suggests newer appliances may ship under a different registrant name, so an absent match here does not rule GE out. Nothing in the sources addresses MAC randomization; a fixed address is the expectation for an appliance but is not documented.
